newsitem.title: USA: Robbins, Ill., incinerator bond tender completed.
newsitem.headline: Robbins, Ill., incinerator bond tender completed.

text.p: The tender of nearly $320 million of Robbins, Ill., resource recovery revenue bonds was completed at 1115 CDT Tuesday, according to a lawyer representing bondholders.

Wendell Adair, an attorney at McDermott, Will & Emery, said the tender of 99.92 percent of the bonds sold in 1994 to finance a waste-to-energy incinerator in the Chicago suburb of Robbins was the highest tender rate that "anyone knows of."
"(The bondholders) are happy campers," he said.

Robbins, in conjunction with Foster Wheeler Corp, the parent company of an Illinois concern that developed the incinerator, initiated the tender offer last month after bondholders tentatively agreed in May to a bond restructuring plan.

Adair said the restructuring lowered the interest rate on the bonds to 8-3/8 percent from 9-1/4 percent. The maturity dates on some of the bonds were also extended and new convenants and different redemption provisions were added.
The restructuring also gave bondholders credit support in the form of Foster Wheeler's guarantee of up to $70 million of earnings from the facility, Adair said.
The bond restructuring was proposed in the wake of the elimination of a state of Illinois subsidy for the Robbins incinerator and two other bond-financed incinerators.
Under a now repealed Illinois law, the state guaranteed incinerators a higher rate at which they could sell their electricity to utilities.
Adair said news of the bond restructuring and subsequent tender has moved bids for the Robbins bonds slightly above par after falling as low as the 60s earlier this year.
Meanwhile, a lawsuit challenging the lost subsidy that was filed by Clinton, N.J.-based Foster Wheeler against state officials is pending in U.S. District Court in Chicago.

A ruling on the state's motion to dismiss the lawsuit on constitutional grounds, which had been expected on Oct. 23, has been indefinitely postponed due to the resignation of Judge Brian Duff, who had been hearing the case. Rick Redmond, an attorney representing the Illinois officials named in the lawsuit, said the case has been reassigned to Judge James Zagel.
Adair said the bond tender was not tied in at all with the lawsuit.
